title: Cottage Cheese & Spinach Stuffed Shells
seoTitle: Cottage Cheese & Spinach Stuffed Shells | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Jumbo pasta shells stuffed with cottage cheese, mozzarella, and spinach in marinara
subtitle: Jumbo pasta shells stuffed with cottage cheese, mozzarella, and spinach in marinara
description: Jumbo pasta shells are stuffed with a cottage cheese, mozzarella, and spinach filling, then baked under marinara until bubbling. It looks and eats like a normal stuffed shells dinner with a genuinely higher protein count per serving.

steps.title: Heat the oven and cook the shells
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Cook jumbo shells in salted boiling water 2 minutes under the package time so they stay firm enough to stuff. Drain and cool slightly. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Build the filling
steps.instruction: In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, 2 cups mozzarella, parmesan, eggs, squeezed spinach, garlic, and Italian seasoning until evenly mixed.

steps.title: Stuff the shells
steps.instruction: Spread 1 cup marinara in the bottom of a 9x13 pan. Stuff each shell with a generous spoonful of filling and arrange seam-side up in the pan.

steps.title: Sauce and top
steps.instruction: Pour remaining marinara over the stuffed shells and scatter the remaining mozzarella on top.

steps.title: Bake covered, then uncovered
steps.instruction: Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10–15 more minutes until bubbling and the cheese on top is golden. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 8–10 minutes before serving so the filling sets and shells hold together on the plate.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover cottage cheese and spinach stuffed shells — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool stuffed shells and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Squeeze spinach in a clean towel, not just a colander — excess water is the main cause of a soupy bake.
Rookie tip: Slightly undercooking the shells before stuffing keeps them from turning mushy after baking.
A piping bag (or a zip-top bag with the corner cut off) makes stuffing the shells much faster for a big batch.
tonightSpread: Main: Cottage cheese and spinach stuffed shells
Sides: Garlic bread, simple green salad
Condiments: Extra parmesan, red pepper flakes
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool cottage cheese and spinach stuffed shells in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Reheat covered at 350°F rather than microwaving so the shells don't turn rubbery.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It keeps the comfort of a baked pasta night while quietly packing more protein than a standard ricotta filling, and it is fully vegetarian without anyone needing to be told.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: assemble the full pan up to a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Storage: refrigerate baked shells up to 4 days. Reheating: cover and reheat at 350°F until warmed through, about 15–20 minutes.
substitutions: Use part-skim ricotta blended half-and-half with cottage cheese for a more traditional texture.
Use frozen chopped kale instead of spinach.
Use a jarred vodka sauce instead of marinara for a richer bake.

adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free pasta. Make your own blend from individually confirmed gluten-free spices, or use a certified gluten-free seasoning packet.
